question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 17 days and B can do the same job in 12 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 2 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 17, 12, and 2 = 204 units.

Efficiency of A = 204 ÷ 17 = 12 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 204 ÷ 12 = 17 units/day.

Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 204 ÷ 2 = 102 units/day.

Efficiency of C = 102 − (12 + 17) = 73 units/day.

Time taken by C alone = 204 ÷ 73 = 2 ⁵⁸/₇₃ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁵⁸/₇₃ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by A = 17 days

⇒ Time taken by B = 12 days

⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together = 2 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of A − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of C = 102 − 12 − 17

⇒ Efficiency of C = 73 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 204 ÷ 73 = 2 ⁵⁸/₇₃ days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁵⁸/₇₃ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work & Efficiency

Total Work = Time × Efficiency. Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken when the total work remains constant.

Pipes & Cisterns

The concept is identical to Time & Work, with the only difference being that filling pipes have a positive efficiency while emptying pipes (or leaks) have a negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the actual amount of work done. If individuals work together for the exact same duration, their wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.
